$comment: EXP-1252 + #EXP-1541 (#FEED-177, #EXP-1536 B3): the device-move picker's per-target refusal, replayed x4 (web apps/web/src/lib/session-device-move.ts `deviceMoveTargetReason` + `visibilityMove`, desktop crates/ui/src/device_move.rs `refusal`, iOS ExpCore SessionDeviceMove.swift `rowBlockedReason`, Android domain/SessionDeviceMove.kt `targetReason`); the server (`lib/sessions/move.ts` `resolveMoveTarget`) reads the same `visibilityMove`. ORDER: offline, then visibility, then no login (no signed-in login of the session's agent there); old builds are the CLIENT_MIN_VERSION floor's job, never a refusal. VISIBILITY: a session keeps its tree's visibility (`shared`) on a move: a target shared with the session's team (`targetShared`) must match it, EXCEPT a QUEUED ROOT with no sub-sessions (`queuedRoot`: status `queued`, no `parentId`, no session under it; nothing ran, its only content is its starter's) moving to one of its STARTER's own machines (`targetIsStarters`: the device row's owner is the session's `userId`; a row without `owner` is the viewer's own): it takes that machine's sharing, exactly as a fresh start there would. A private session never lands on a teammate's box, and only its starter (`moverIsStarter`: the viewer is the session's `userId`) may make a shared session private. `visibilityCases` = the pure rule (expected = the visibility it has there, null = refused); `queuedRootCases` = when a session counts as a queued root; `targetCases` = the whole refusal from a device row + a session + the viewer (`deviceOwner` = the row's owner id; it equals `mover` for the viewer's own row, which then carries no `owner`), expected = a `reasons` key or null (movable).

reasons.visibility: This device is shared differently, so the session can't move here.
reasons.noLogin: This device has no signed-in login for this agent.

visibilityCases.name: a queued root adopts its starter's shared machine
a queued root adopts its starter's personal machine
a teammate may take a private queued root onto its starter's shared machine
a live or crowded tree keeps the strict rule
only the starter makes a shared session private

targetCases.name: FEED-177: a queued root moves to its starter's shared machine
a running session keeps the strict rule
a shared queued root moves to its starter's personal machine
a teammate never makes a shared session private
a private queued root never lands on a teammate's machine
a teammate's shared machine takes a shared session
the visibility passes, then no login
